body: A Cumberland County judge heard arguments on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, on a legal challenge intended to stop the PAX-1 data center development in Middlesex Township, WITF reported. Stop PAX-1, a group of residents opposed to the $15 billion project, has filed three legal challenges to it. WITF's report describes a substantive validity challenge to the township's data center zoning, and its subhead says the residents are suing the developer and asking a judge to halt construction. abc27 earlier reported that the judge declined to order construction stopped and set the Nov. 13 hearing.

According to WITF, the residents' attorney argued for a stay on development of the phases already approved and a pause on future approvals. The attorney for the developer, which WITF names as Pennsylvania Data Center Partners, moved to dismiss the case and argued that the request for a stay was filed too late. abc27's reports name the developer as Carlisle Development Partners. The judge did not rule immediately after the arguments.

PAX-1 would include 16 data center buildings on 693 acres, WITF reported. Middlesex Township officials gave final approval to the first phase in September, and final approval votes for the next two phases are planned for February.

timeline.label: Middlesex Township officials give final approval to the first phase of PAX-1
Judge hears arguments on the residents' stay request and the developer's motion to dismiss; no ruling
